item.title: Martin Wolf on the US midterms: Trump loses. European populism lives on.
item.itunes:title: Martin Wolf on the US midterms: Trump loses. European populism lives on.
item.itunes:subtitle: Timothy Garton Ash on why Europe’s populist right may well outlast Trump
item.description:
Before the 2026 midterms, Timothy Garton Ash, emeritus professor of European studies at the University of Oxford and author of ‘Europe in 7½ Chapters’, described the elections as a crucial test of US democracy. Now, with the Democrats’ sweeping victory, could the tide be turning against rightwing populism on both sides of the Atlantic or will Europe’s nationalist parties continue to gain ground? Garton Ash and Martin Wolf discuss the common factors between European nationalists, what European politicians can learn from a Democrat victory and whether there’s reason to hope for the future of liberal democracy.


To enjoy future episodes, be sure to subscribe to ‘Martin Wolf on the World’ wherever you get your podcasts. You can also watch Martin’s podcast series on the FT’s YouTube channel here: https://www.youtube.com/@FinancialTimes

item.title: Nvidia after Jensen Huang
item.itunes:title: Nvidia after Jensen Huang
item.itunes:subtitle: Co-founder and CEO’s departure raises big questions about the company’’s future
item.description:
Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO. We look at what it means for the company, AI sector, stock market and the US government’s relationship with China. Plus, European leaders reject Vladimir Putin’s push to overhaul the continent’s security architecture as part of Ukraine peace talks.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Jensen Huang resigns as chief executive after affair allegations

Meet the contenders to succeed Jensen Huang

Jensen Huang is gone. Will the AI industry pay the price?

Nvidia sends a painful message on how to value a CEO

European leaders reject Russian push to overhaul continent’s security

Ukraine says Starlink restrictions are back as US envoys land in Moscow

item.title: Nvidia board meets to discuss Huang’s future
item.itunes:title: Nvidia board meets to discuss Huang’s future
item.itunes:subtitle: Nvidia CEO’s future uncertain as board holds urgent talks after revelations of second affair
item.description:
Nvidia’s board is holding urgent talks about the future of its founder Jensen Huang after revelations that he had an affair with a top executive at the company. European leaders meet in Dublin today to reheat an interminable debate over how to speak to Russia. Plus, Spain’s first general strike in 14 years disrupted transport, factories and public services, and US prosecutors allege an attempt to attack a British air base was partly directed by an Iranian-Iraqi national from a New York jail.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Nvidia board set to meet after revelations Jensen Huang had affair with top company executive

Europe dithers over who and how to talk to Putin amid US and Ukraine pressure

Spain roiled by first general strike in 14 years

item.title: A look at the alleged spy who had an affair with Nvidia’s CEO
item.itunes:title: A look at the alleged spy who had an affair with Nvidia’s CEO
item.itunes:subtitle: Alice Huang conducted business meetings with her purported husband, who has been fined multiple times for financial violations
item.description:
Anthropic is targeting a valuation of $1.4tn in its initial public offering, stronger than expected inflation data sparked fresh bets that the Federal Reserve will increase interest rates next month, and France is pressing Germany to define how it would use long-range missiles in the event of a conflict with Russia. Plus, we take a microscope to Alice Huang, the woman who US officials believe is a Chinese spy and had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4tn in IPO

Treasuries slide as ‘hot’ inflation sparks bets on Fed rate rise

Alice Huang’s tangled web of connections

France pressures Germany over nuclear risks of long-range missiles

item.title: The fallout of Nvidia’s spying scandal
item.itunes:title: The fallout of Nvidia’s spying scandal
item.itunes:subtitle: Chief executive’s affair sends shares falling
item.description:
Nvidia shares tumbled after the company’s board said it would investigate reports that chief executive Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign espionage operation, investors are buying up stocks they believe can protect them in a market downturn, and BT will not launch its partnership with Elon Musk’s Starlink. Plus, the FT sat down with Britain’s defence secretary Wes Streeting to discuss UK-Russia relations.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Nvidia shares fall as it probes alleged Chinese spy scandal

US stocks rebound after AI rout

Investors pile into defensive stocks amid fears AI bull market may be over

Russian strikes aim to cut Ukraine in half, Zelenskyy warns

US-Russia-Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi

UK and Russia must seek communication channels to avoid escalation, says Streeting

BT cools on Starlink satellite tie-up after Elon Musk Ukraine controversy

Republican lawmaker moves to impeach US defence secretary Pete Hegseth

item.title: Nvidia CEO admits to affair after allegations of relationship with Chinese spy
item.itunes:title: Nvidia CEO admits to affair after allegations of relationship with Chinese spy
item.itunes:subtitle: Tech company opens investigation into Jensen Huang
item.description:
Nvidia is investigating whether chief executive Jensen Huang was “the target of a foreign intelligence effort,” Israel’s president has formally given Gadi Eisenkot the first chance at forming a new government, and the FT’s Chris Giles sat down with Klaas Knot, who is vying for the top job at the European Central Bank. Plus, foreign buyers are snapping up British companies, and a Dutch start-up founded by former Palantir alumni has a plan to awaken Europe’s defence industry.


Mentioned in this podcast:

US believes Nvidia’s Huang had romantic relationship with alleged Chinese spy

Israel’s president gives Gadi Eisenkot first chance at forming a government
